extracted.intended_audience: K08 grant reviewers and early-career transplant surgeon-scientists preparing NIH K08 career-development applications
extracted.subtask_description: A K08 career development and research plan for an early-career transplant surgeon-scientist proposing preclinical studies (rat NEVLP model) to expand regulatory dendritic cells (DCregs) and reduce liver transplant rejection, plus training/mentorship and benchmark milestones toward an R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development and Leadership Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: I will attend the UW Institute for Clinical and Translational Research (ICTR) career development seminars and complete a customized mentee training curriculum through the UW-Madison Center for the Improvement of Mentored Experiences in Research. ... I will take the 3-day American College of Surgeons (ACS) Surgeons as Leaders course in Year 2 of the award. ... attend the daylong Leadership and Management Development Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly career development discussions with mentors; expand leadership skills via formal courses; training should be relevant for early career scientists (research methods, bioinformatics, core service technologies, leadership) and complement mentor meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct in Research
rubrics_metrics.description: I will enroll in Pharmacy 800 (Research Ethics, Scientific Integrity and the Responsible Conduct of Research), which is approved by the Office of Research Integrity and meets the NIH requirements for the responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course consists of face-to-face faculty instruction via presentations and case discussion; discuss RCR training with mentors during semi-annual meetings; mentor ensures ongoing updates and availability to discuss ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Benchmarks for Successful Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve my ultimate goal of developing an independent research laboratory, by the end of this K08 award, I will generate a competitive R01 application. In Year 4, participate in a K to R grant writing workshop; in Years 4-5 prepare and submit an R01. Actively seek speaking engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The R01 submission is the largest benchmark and important for promotion to the tenure track; publications and conference presentations are milestones of progression to expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and Scholarly Productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: I will submit research abstracts (average two per year) and present at annual meetings (American Transplant Congress, Great Lakes Transplant Immunology Forum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conferences to form collaborations and complement efforts cultivated at home institution; track manuscripts and conference presentations in timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Project must address a major unmet need: development of innovative strategies to decrease rejection of the transplanted liver and minimize lifelong dangerous anti-rejection drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide epidemiologic context and prior evidence that acute rejection harms graft and patient survival; justify clinical relevance and potential immediate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two major innovations: (1) novel therapeutic strategies to alter the phenotype of liver-resident DCregs prior to transplantation; (2) novel use of NEVLP as a delivery method to modulate cells within the organ ex vivo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue novelty relative to prior DCreg in vitro expansion protocols and emphasize translational potential using clinically-available NEVLP technology and reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Hypothesis and Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear central hypothesis: expansion of liver-resident DCregs during NEVLP will promote a regulatory environment for the organ after transplant through expression of co-inhibitory proteins and production of regulatory EVs. Two defined aims test mechanism (Aim 1) and therapeutic impact (Aim 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State working hypotheses explicitly, link aims to hypothesis, and outline experimental tests and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Model Rigor and Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The rat experimental system will be used because all antibodies and cytokine detection supplies are commercially available, and it is an established, reproducible liver transplant model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticate key biological resources; use established strain pairs (LEW and BN) where rejection vs tolerance is known to reduce confounding; document reagents and validation to support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Relevant Biological Variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender will be randomly assigned for both donor and recipient. Female and male BN rats will be donors and female and male LEW rats will be recipients. Rats will be approximately 10-12 weeks of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomly assign sex to avoid bias; state age and rationale for selection; address sex as a biological variable in experimental design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized NEVLP Protocol and Unbiased Experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducted standardized NEVLP experiments on randomly selected, 10-12-week-old, male and female rats to obtain robust, unbiased results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement standardized perfusion procedures; random selection of animals for NEVLP groups to reduce selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic Perturbations to Test Causality
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine mechanisms of DCreg immune inhibition, treat animals with GW4869 to inhibit EV production and with anti-PD-L1 antibody to block PD-L1+ DCregs (one day prior to procurement/transplant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pharmacologic inhibitors and blocking antibodies timed appropriately to interrogate specific mechanisms; include both EV-inhibition and PD-L1 blockade arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative Strain Models (Controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LEW to BN (rejecting) and BN to LEW (non-rejecting) transplant models to investigate DCreg contribution to rejection vs tolerance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage known donor-recipient combinations (allogeneic strains) so one combination reliably rejects and the other is tolerant; use comparisons to identify mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome and Endpoint Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and secondary outcomes include survival (long-term observations), peripheral blood markers (total bilirubin, AST), liver-type injury markers via multiplex Luminex, flow cytometry phenotypes of lymphocytes, EV characterization (cell of origin, size distribution, concentration by Nanosight), and histologic rejection activity index (Banff scoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect serial blood samples weekly, pre-determined euthanasia timepoints (5,10,20 days), and perform multiparameter assays in triplicate; use multiple complementary readouts (functional, biochemical, cellular, histologic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Histopathologic Assessment Using Standardized Scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: At endpoint, a portion of liver will be fixed and stained for assessment of the rejection activity index according to the Banff scoring schema by an independent histopathologist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated, field-standard histologic scoring (Banff) and independent pathologist review to enhance objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Size, Power Calculation, and Statistical Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size calculations assume a difference in means of 20% with SD 15%; alpha 0.05 and power 80% yield 9 animals per group. Multiplex assays in triplicate. For continuous variables use paired t-test if normal or rank-sum if non-normal; categorical by Fischer's exact test. P<0.05 considered significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit assumptions for effect size and variability, pre-specify statistical tests, replicate multiplex assays, and predefine significance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Multiple Assays and Technical Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiparameter flow cytometry to phenotype cells, Nanosight for EV sizing/quantification, multiplex Luminex assays for liver injury markers, and fluorescence microscopy for labeled DCreg tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate findings across orthogonal methods; run appropriate controls (e.g., fluorescence minus one gating) and replicate measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data and Rationale for Interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data show anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-10, TGFβ) decrease expression of MHC class II and trend toward decreasing CD40 on DCregs during NEVLP; Flt3-L injection increases DCreg frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary results to justify choice of cytokines, dosing strategies, and expansion approaches; show prior evidence of feasibility and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Pitfalls and Alternative Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated issues include tolerance not solely dependent on DCregs or DCregs failing to decrease rejection. Alternatives: systematically deplete passenger lymphocytes to identify required cells; target alternative cells for expansion if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively list potential negative outcomes and concrete alternative experiments to address them; be explicit about backup plans if primary approach fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational Relevance / Use of Clinically Available Platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilization of clinically available NEVLP technology and reagents could lead to immediate clinical application; concept may generalize to other organs (lung, kidney) where normothermic perfusion is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize use of clinically-relevant platforms and reagents to support near-term translational potential and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in Research Administration and Mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in customized mentor training curricula at UW Center for the Improvement of Mentored Experiences in Research in years 3-5; hold discussions with mentors who have managed successful labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gain laboratory management and operational skills, communication, fostering independence of lab members, and ethical leadership by leveraging mentor experience and formal curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking Timeline and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 2 summarizes research and training activities across Years 1–5, including courses, conferences, grant submissions (Wisconsin Partnership Program, K-to-R workshop, NIH R01 submission), publications and presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a year-by-year timeline with scheduled training, experiments, and grant-writing milestones; use timeline to demonstrate feasibility and planning.
